claim: Fam20C is the physiological Golgi casein kinase, which phosphorylates many secreted proteins and is critical for proper biomineralization.
source: Fam20C is the physiological Golgi casein kinase, which phosphorylates many secreted proteins and is critical for proper biomineralization.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work establishing Fam20C's role, and is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Fam20A is essential for enamel formation.
source: Fam20A, a Fam20C paralog, is essential for enamel formation, but the biochemical function of Fam20A is unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations in the introduction discussing Fam20A mutations causing amelogenesis imperfecta.

claim: The biochemical function of Fam20A was unknown prior to this study.
source: Fam20A, a Fam20C paralog, is essential for enamel formation, but the biochemical function of Fam20A is unknown.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as the knowledge gap addressed by the study.

claim: Fam20A potentiates Fam20C kinase activity in vitro.
source: Here we show that Fam20A potentiates Fam20C kinase activity and promotes the phosphorylation of enamel matrix proteins in vitro and in cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in vitro kinase assays shown in the manuscript.

claim: Fam20A promotes the phosphorylation of enamel matrix proteins in vitro and in cells.
source: Here we show that Fam20A potentiates Fam20C kinase activity and promotes the phosphorylation of enamel matrix proteins in vitro and in cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Fam20A is a pseudokinase.
source: Mechanistically, Fam20A is a pseudokinase that forms a functional complex with Fam20C, and this complex enhances extracellular protein phosphorylation within the secretory pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing Fam20A lacks catalytic activity and lacks a critical catalytic residue.

claim: Fam20A forms a functional complex with Fam20C.
source: Mechanistically, Fam20A is a pseudokinase that forms a functional complex with Fam20C, and this complex enhances extracellular protein phosphorylation within the secretory pathway.
evidence: This is supported by gel filtration, co-immunoprecipitation, and analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: The Fam20A/Fam20C complex enhances extracellular protein phosphorylation within the secretory pathway.
source: Mechanistically, Fam20A is a pseudokinase that forms a functional complex with Fam20C, and this complex enhances extracellular protein phosphorylation within the secretory pathway.
evidence: This is supported by cellular phosphorylation assays and in vitro kinase assays.

claim: Numerous extracellular phosphoproteins have been identified.
source: Although numerous extracellular phosphoproteins have been identified, the protein kinases within the secretory pathway have only recently been discovered, and their regulation is virtually unexplored.
evidence: This is supported by citations to phosphoproteomic studies.

claim: Protein kinases within the secretory pathway have only recently been discovered.
source: Although numerous extracellular phosphoproteins have been identified, the protein kinases within the secretory pathway have only recently been discovered, and their regulation is virtually unexplored.
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent discovery papers.

claim: The regulation of secretory pathway kinases is virtually unexplored.
source: Although numerous extracellular phosphoproteins have been identified, the protein kinases within the secretory pathway have only recently been discovered, and their regulation is virtually unexplored.
evidence: This is stated as the knowledge gap and is based on the lack of prior literature.

claim: Fam20C was identified as the long-sought Golgi casein kinase.
source: Fam20C was identified as the long-sought Golgi casein kinase, which phosphorylates secreted proteins within Ser-x-Glu/phospho-Ser (SxE/pS) motifs, including casein and members of the secretory calcium binding phosphoprotein (SCPP) family (Kawasaki and Weiss, 2008; Tagliabracci et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Fam20C phosphorylates secreted proteins within Ser-x-Glu/phospho-Ser (SxE/pS) motifs.
source: Fam20C was identified as the long-sought Golgi casein kinase, which phosphorylates secreted proteins within Ser-x-Glu/phospho-Ser (SxE/pS) motifs, including casein and members of the secretory calcium binding phosphoprotein (SCPP) family (Kawasaki and Weiss, 2008; Tagliabracci et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and confirmed by data in this manuscript.

claim: Fam20C phosphorylates casein.
source: Fam20C was identified as the long-sought Golgi casein kinase, which phosphorylates secreted proteins within Ser-x-Glu/phospho-Ser (SxE/pS) motifs, including casein and members of the secretory calcium binding phosphoprotein (SCPP) family (Kawasaki and Weiss, 2008; Tagliabracci et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Fam20C phosphorylates members of the secretory calcium binding phosphoprotein (SCPP) family.
source: Fam20C was identified as the long-sought Golgi casein kinase, which phosphorylates secreted proteins within Ser-x-Glu/phospho-Ser (SxE/pS) motifs, including casein and members of the secretory calcium binding phosphoprotein (SCPP) family (Kawasaki and Weiss, 2008; Tagliabracci et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and data in this manuscript.

claim: Some 75% of phosphoproteins identified in human serum and cerebrospinal fluid contain phosphate within the Fam20C consensus sequence.
source: Furthermore, some 75% of phosphoproteins identified in human serum and cerebrospinal fluid contain phosphate within the Fam20C consensus sequence, suggesting that Fam20C may have a broad spectrum of substrates and therefore play a major role in establishing the secreted phosphoproteome (Bahl et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2009; Salvi et al., 2010; Tagliabracci et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to phosphoproteomic studies.

claim: Fam20C may have a broad spectrum of substrates.
source: Furthermore, some 75% of phosphoproteins identified in human serum and cerebrospinal fluid contain phosphate within the Fam20C consensus sequence, suggesting that Fam20C may have a broad spectrum of substrates and therefore play a major role in establishing the secreted phosphoproteome (Bahl et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2009; Salvi et al., 2010; Tagliabracci et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the high percentage of phosphoproteins containing the Fam20C consensus sequence.

claim: Fam20C may play a major role in establishing the secreted phosphoproteome.
source: Furthermore, some 75% of phosphoproteins identified in human serum and cerebrospinal fluid contain phosphate within the Fam20C consensus sequence, suggesting that Fam20C may have a broad spectrum of substrates and therefore play a major role in establishing the secreted phosphoproteome (Bahl et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2009; Salvi et al., 2010; Tagliabracci et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the high percentage of phosphoproteins containing the Fam20C consensus sequence.

claim: How Fam20C is regulated is unknown.
source: Nonetheless, how Fam20C is regulated is unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap.

claim: Fj phosphorylates extracellular cadherin domains.
source: In addition to Fam20C, Fj, the founding member of the family, phosphorylates extracellular cadherin domains (Ishikawa et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Fam20B phosphorylates xylose within a tetrasaccharide linkage region of O-linked proteoglycans.
source: Fam20B phosphorylates xylose within a tetrasaccharide linkage region of O-linked proteoglycans and functions to promote glycosaminoglycan chain elongation (Koike et al., 2009; Wen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Fam20B functions to promote glycosaminoglycan chain elongation.
source: Fam20B phosphorylates xylose within a tetrasaccharide linkage region of O-linked proteoglycans and functions to promote glycosaminoglycan chain elongation (Koike et al., 2009; Wen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Both Fam20C and Fam20A are implicated in biomineralization.
source: Both Fam20C and Fam20A are implicated in biomineralization.
evidence: This is supported by citations to human genetic studies and mouse models.

claim: Fam20C deficiency in humans is associated with a severe and often lethal osteosclerotic bone dysplasia known as Raine syndrome.
source: Fam20C deficiency in humans is associated with a severe and often lethal osteosclerotic bone dysplasia known as Raine syndrome (Simpson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a clinical study.

claim: Patients with non-lethal forms of Raine syndrome exhibit hypophosphatemia, ectopic calcifications and dental anomalies.
source: Patients with non-lethal forms of Raine syndrome exhibit hypophosphatemia, ectopic calcifications and dental anomalies (Simpson et al., 2009; Fradin et al., 2011; Rafaelsen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Patients with non-lethal Raine syndrome have misformed dentin and enamel.
source: These patients have misformed dentin and enamel, suggesting that Fam20C is essential for dentinogenesis and amelogenesis (Fradin et al., 2011; Rafaelsen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Fam20C is essential for dentinogenesis and amelogenesis.
source: These patients have misformed dentin and enamel, suggesting that Fam20C is essential for dentinogenesis and amelogenesis (Fradin et al., 2011; Rafaelsen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from clinical observations in patients with Fam20C mutations.

claim: Patients with FAM20A gene mutations develop disorders of enamel formation referred to as Amelogenesis Imperfecta (AI).
source: Furthermore, patients with FAM20A gene mutations also develop disorders of enamel formation referred to as Amelogenesis Imperfecta (AI), which is often accompanied by ectopic calcification, such as nephrocalcinosis (O'Sullivan et al., 2011; Cho et al., 2012; Jaureguiberry et al., 2012; Cabral et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2013a, 2014; Kantaputra et al., 2014a, 2014b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Amelogenesis Imperfecta caused by FAM20A mutations is often accompanied by ectopic calcification, such as nephrocalcinosis.
source: Furthermore, patients with FAM20A gene mutations also develop disorders of enamel formation referred to as Amelogenesis Imperfecta (AI), which is often accompanied by ectopic calcification, such as nephrocalcinosis (O'Sullivan et al., 2011; Cho et al., 2012; Jaureguiberry et al., 2012; Cabral et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2013a, 2014; Kantaputra et al., 2014a, 2014b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Both Fam20A-knockout (KO) and Fam20C-KO mouse models exhibit similar enamel phenotypes.
source: Notably, both Fam20A-knockout (KO) and Fam20C-KO mouse models have been generated and they exhibit similar enamel phenotypes, suggesting that Fam20A and Fam20C might function in the same pathway to control enamel formation (Vogel et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2012, 2013c).
evidence: This is supported by citations to mouse model studies.

claim: Fam20A and Fam20C might function in the same pathway to control enamel formation.
source: Notably, both Fam20A-knockout (KO) and Fam20C-KO mouse models have been generated and they exhibit similar enamel phenotypes, suggesting that Fam20A and Fam20C might function in the same pathway to control enamel formation (Vogel et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2012, 2013c).
evidence: This is inferred from the similar phenotypes of the knockout mice.

claim: AI can be caused by a missense mutation in the secreted protein enamelin (ENAM) that disrupts phosphorylation within an SxE motif.
source: Further evidence to support a role for extracellular protein phosphorylation in the regulation of enamel formation comes from the discovery that AI can be caused by a missense mutation in the secreted protein enamelin (ENAM) that disrupts phosphorylation within an SxE motif (Chan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a clinical study.

claim: ENAM is an enamel matrix protein.
source: ENAM is an enamel matrix protein that, together with amelogenin X (AMELX), ameloblastin (AMBN) and amelotin (AMTN), makes up a subfamily of the SCPPs (Kawasaki and Weiss, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: AMELX, AMBN, AMTN, and ENAM make up a subfamily of the SCPPs.
source: ENAM is an enamel matrix protein that, together with amelogenin X (AMELX), ameloblastin (AMBN) and amelotin (AMTN), makes up a subfamily of the SCPPs (Kawasaki and Weiss, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Enamel matrix proteins are secreted from specialized cells known as ameloblasts.
source: These proteins are secreted from specialized cells known as ameloblasts and act as a scaffold for enamel calcification (Hu et al., 2007; Moradian-Oldak, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Enamel matrix proteins act as a scaffold for enamel calcification.
source: These proteins are secreted from specialized cells known as ameloblasts and act as a scaffold for enamel calcification (Hu et al., 2007; Moradian-Oldak, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ENAM, AMELX, AMBN and AMTN are all phosphorylated within SxE motifs.
source: ENAM, AMELX, AMBN and AMTN are all phosphorylated within SxE motifs and are therefore potential Fam20C substrates (Kawasaki and Weiss, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ENAM, AMELX, AMBN and AMTN are potential Fam20C substrates.
source: ENAM, AMELX, AMBN and AMTN are all phosphorylated within SxE motifs and are therefore potential Fam20C substrates (Kawasaki and Weiss, 2008).
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that they contain SxE motifs and Fam20C phosphorylates SxE motifs.

claim: Phosphorylation within a conserved SxE motif in AMELX appears to be important for enamel mineralization.
source: In addition to ENAM phosphorylation, phosphorylation within a conserved SxE motif in AMELX also appears to be important for enamel mineralization (Kwak et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Fam20C phosphorylates AMELX in vitro.
source: Recombinant Fam20C phosphorylated each of these proteins in a time-dependent manner in vitro, whereas an inactive Fam20C D478A mutant did not (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Fam20C phosphorylates AMTN in vitro.
source: Recombinant Fam20C phosphorylated each of these proteins in a time-dependent manner in vitro, whereas an inactive Fam20C D478A mutant did not (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Fam20C phosphorylates ENAM (173-277) in vitro.
source: Recombinant Fam20C phosphorylated each of these proteins in a time-dependent manner in vitro, whereas an inactive Fam20C D478A mutant did not (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Inactive Fam20C D478A mutant does not phosphorylate enamel matrix proteins in vitro.
source: Recombinant Fam20C phosphorylated each of these proteins in a time-dependent manner in vitro, whereas an inactive Fam20C D478A mutant did not (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ENAM (173-277) contains two SxE motifs (S191 and S216).
source: ENAM (173–277) contains two SxE motifs (S191 and S216), both of which are highly conserved and known to be phosphorylated (Fukae et al., 1996; Al-Hashimi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Both S191 and S216 in ENAM are highly conserved and known to be phosphorylated.
source: ENAM (173–277) contains two SxE motifs (S191 and S216), both of which are highly conserved and known to be phosphorylated (Fukae et al., 1996; Al-Hashimi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A S216L mutation in ENAM causes AI.
source: As mentioned above, a S216L mutation causes AI (Chan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a clinical study.

claim: Fam20C phosphorylates ENAM (173-277) on S191 and S216.
source: Thus, Fam20C phosphorylates ENAM (173–277) on S191 and S216.
evidence: This is demonstrated by mutagenesis experiments shown in Figure 1B.

claim: ENAM S191A mutant exhibits markedly reduced phosphorylation by Fam20C.
source: As shown in Figure 1B, both the S191A and S216L ENAM mutants exhibited markedly reduced phosphorylation by Fam20C.
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 1B.

claim: ENAM S216L mutant exhibits markedly reduced phosphorylation by Fam20C.
source: As shown in Figure 1B, both the S191A and S216L ENAM mutants exhibited markedly reduced phosphorylation by Fam20C.
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mutation of both S191 and S216 in ENAM completely abolished Fam20C-dependent phosphorylation.
source: Further, mutation of both Ser residues completely abolished Fam20C-dependent phosphorylation (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Disruption of Fam20C completely eliminated AMBN phosphorylation in ameloblast-like cells.
source: Disruption of Fam20C completely eliminated AMBN phosphorylation, suggesting that Fam20C is the kinase that phosphorylates enamel matrix proteins in vivo (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by metabolic labeling experiments in Fam20C-KO cells shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Fam20C is the kinase that phosphorylates enamel matrix proteins in vivo.
source: Disruption of Fam20C completely eliminated AMBN phosphorylation, suggesting that Fam20C is the kinase that phosphorylates enamel matrix proteins in vivo (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is inferred from the complete loss of AMBN phosphorylation in Fam20C-KO cells.

claim: Recombinant Fam20A was unable to phosphorylate enamel proteins in vitro.
source: However, recombinant Fam20A was unable to phosphorylate the enamel proteins in vitro (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Fam20A was unable to phosphorylate any protein or carbohydrate substrates tested.
source: In fact, Fam20A was unable to phosphorylate any protein or carbohydrate substrates we tested, raising the question of whether Fam20A is an active kinase.
evidence: This is based on experimental testing of multiple substrates.

claim: Fam20C exhibits intrinsic ATPase activity.
source: Incubation of recombinant Fam20C with ATP resulted in the time-dependent release of phosphate, which correlated with the kinase activity of Fam20C (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ATPase assays shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Fam20A was unable to hydrolyze ATP.
source: In contrast, Fam20A was unable to hydrolyze ATP (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ATPase assays shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The Tm of Fam20C significantly increased in the presence of ATP.
source: As expected, the Tm of Fam20C significantly increased in the presence of ATP, whereas the Tm of maltose-binding protein (MBP) was unchanged (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by thermal stability shift assays shown in Figure 2B.

claim: An increase in the thermal stability of Fam20A was observed in the presence of ATP.
source: We also observed an increase in the thermal stability of Fam20A in the presence of ATP, suggesting that Fam20A binds ATP (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by thermal stability shift assays shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Fam20A binds ATP.
source: We also observed an increase in the thermal stability of Fam20A in the presence of ATP, suggesting that Fam20A binds ATP (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is inferred from the increase in thermal stability in the presence of ATP.

claim: Most of the residues important for Fam20C activity are conserved in Fam20A, including the metal-binding Asp (D478 in human Fam20C), the catalytic Asp (D458 in human Fam20C), and the ion pair (K285 and E311 in human Fam20C).
source: Most of the residues important for Fam20C activity are conserved in Fam20A, including the metal-binding Asp (D478 in human Fam20C), the catalytic Asp (D458 in human Fam20C), and the ion pair (K285 and E311 in human Fam20C) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A conserved Glu in Fam20C (E306 in human) is replaced by a Gln (Q258 in human) in all Fam20A orthologs.
source: However, a conserved Glu in Fam20C (E306 in human), which coordinates the Mn2+ ion and the ion-pair Lys and is indispensable for Fam20C kinase activity, is replaced by a Gln (Q258 in human) in all Fam20A orthologs (Figure 2C,D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and [Xiao et al., 2013]).
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment and structural analysis.

claim: E306 in Fam20C coordinates the Mn2+ ion and the ion-pair Lys and is indispensable for Fam20C kinase activity.
source: However, a conserved Glu in Fam20C (E306 in human), which coordinates the Mn2+ ion and the ion-pair Lys and is indispensable for Fam20C kinase activity, is replaced by a Gln (Q258 in human) in all Fam20A orthologs (Figure 2C,D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and [Xiao et al., 2013]).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis and citation to prior work.

claim: Recombinant Fam20C E306Q exhibited greatly reduced in vitro kinase activity towards casein, ENAM (173-277), and osteopontin (OPN) as compared to WT Fam20C.
source: Recombinant Fam20C E306Q exhibited greatly reduced in vitro kinase activity towards casein, ENAM (173–277), as well as osteopontin (OPN), an SCPP and model substrate of Fam20C, as compared to WT Fam20C (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The intrinsic ATPase activity of Fam20C E306Q was abolished.
source: Accordingly, the intrinsic ATPase activity of Fam20C E306Q was abolished (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ATPase assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Fam20A Q258E was able to hydrolyze ATP.
source: Conversely, Fam20A Q258E was able to hydrolyze ATP and phosphorylate OPN, albeit less robustly than Fam20C (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ATPase assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Fam20A Q258E was able to phosphorylate OPN, albeit less robustly than Fam20C.
source: Conversely, Fam20A Q258E was able to hydrolyze ATP and phosphorylate OPN, albeit less robustly than Fam20C (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by kinase assays shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Fam20A does not have all the residues essential for catalytic activity.
source: These data suggest that Fam20A does not have all the residues essential for catalytic activity and that Fam20A is not an intrinsically active kinase.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutagenesis experiments showing that Q258E partially restores activity.

claim: Fam20A is not an intrinsically active kinase.
source: These data suggest that Fam20A does not have all the residues essential for catalytic activity and that Fam20A is not an intrinsically active kinase.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of ATPase and kinase activity.

claim: V5-tagged AMBN phosphorylation was greatly diminished in Fam20A-KO ALCs.
source: Although Fam20A is likely catalytically inactive, we observed that V5-tagged AMBN phosphorylation was greatly diminished in Fam20A-KO ALCs (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by metabolic labeling experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Phosphorylation of V5-tagged OPN was dramatically reduced in Fam20A-KO ALCs.
source: This effect was not solely restricted to enamel proteins because phosphorylation of V5-tagged OPN was also dramatically reduced in Fam20A-KO ALCs (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by metabolic labeling experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Reintroduction of Flag-tagged Fam20A in Fam20A-KO ALCs restored the phosphorylation of V5-tagged AMBN and OPN.
source: Reintroduction of Flag-tagged Fam20A in Fam20A-KO ALCs restored the phosphorylation of V5-tagged AMBN and OPN (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rescue experiments shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: The phosphorylation of V5-tagged OPN was totally eliminated when the Fam20c gene was disrupted in either WT or Fam20A-KO cells.
source: Notably, the phosphorylation of V5-tagged OPN was totally eliminated when the Fam20c gene was disrupted in either WT or Fam20A-KO cells (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by metabolic labeling experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Ectopic expression of Fam20A in U2OS cells significantly increased phosphorylation of V5-tagged OPN, ENAM and AMBN.
source: Furthermore, ectopic expression of Fam20A in the human osteosarcoma cell line U2OS, which produces Fam20C, but not Fam20A, significantly increased phosphorylation of V5-tagged OPN, ENAM and AMBN, without altering Fam20C expression levels (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by metabolic labeling experiments shown in Figures 3D-F.

claim: U2OS cells produce Fam20C, but not Fam20A.
source: Furthermore, ectopic expression of Fam20A in the human osteosarcoma cell line U2OS, which produces Fam20C, but not Fam20A, significantly increased phosphorylation of V5-tagged OPN, ENAM and AMBN, without altering Fam20C expression levels (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the cell line used.

claim: Ectopic expression of Fam20A in U2OS cells did not alter Fam20C expression levels.
source: Furthermore, ectopic expression of Fam20A in the human osteosarcoma cell line U2OS, which produces Fam20C, but not Fam20A, significantly increased phosphorylation of V5-tagged OPN, ENAM and AMBN, without altering Fam20C expression levels (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis shown in Figures 3D-F.

claim: No phosphorylation of OPN, ENAM, or AMBN was detected in Fam20C-KO U2OS cells, even when Flag-tagged Fam20A was overexpressed.
source: In contrast, no phosphorylation of these substrates was detected in Fam20C-KO U2OS cells, even when Flag-tagged Fam20A was overexpressed (Figure 3D–F and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by metabolic labeling experiments shown in Figures 3D-F.

claim: Fam20A functions to increase Fam20C substrate phosphorylation when Fam20C is present.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that Fam20A functions to increase Fam20C substrate phosphorylation when Fam20C is present.
evidence: This is inferred from the cellular experiments showing Fam20A enhances phosphorylation only when Fam20C is present.

claim: When both Fam20A and Fam20C were incubated in the reactions, phosphorylation of ENAM, AMTN, or SUMO-AMBN-N were all greatly increased.
source: When both proteins were incubated in the reactions, phosphorylation of ENAM, AMTN, or an N-terminal peptide of AMBN fused to a SUMO tag (SUMO-AMBN-N), were all greatly increased (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Recombinant Fam20B did not increase Fam20C-catalyzed ENAM phosphorylation.
source: Recombinant Fam20B did not increase Fam20C-catalyzed ENAM phosphorylation (Figure 4B), nor did Fam20A or Fam20C have any effect on Fam20B-catalyzed xylose phosphorylation of the proteoglycan decorin (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Fam20A or Fam20C did not have any effect on Fam20B-catalyzed xylose phosphorylation of the proteoglycan decorin.
source: Recombinant Fam20B did not increase Fam20C-catalyzed ENAM phosphorylation (Figure 4B), nor did Fam20A or Fam20C have any effect on Fam20B-catalyzed xylose phosphorylation of the proteoglycan decorin (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The activating effect of Fam20A is specific to Fam20C substrate phosphorylation.
source: These results suggest that the activating effect of Fam20A is specific to Fam20C substrate phosphorylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the specificity experiments with Fam20B.

claim: In the presence of Fam20A, ENAM (173-277) was readily phosphorylated by Fam20C.
source: When both Fam20A and Fam20C were included in the reactions, ENAM (173–277) was readily phosphorylated.
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The ENAM S191A/S216L double mutant was not phosphorylated by Fam20C even in the presence of Fam20A.
source: However, the S191A/S216L double mutant was not, even though it contains 21 additional Ser/Thr/Tyr residues (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The phosphorylation remains specific to SxE motifs in the presence of Fam20A.
source: These results demonstrate that the phosphorylation remains specific to SxE motifs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by mutagenesis experiments showing only SxE sites are phosphorylated.

claim: The kinase activity of Fam20C is indispensable for substrate phosphorylation in the presence of Fam20A.
source: As anticipated, the kinase activity of Fam20C was indispensable (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments using kinase-dead Fam20C mutants.

claim: Fam20A functions as an activator of Fam20C kinase activity.
source: These results point to a model where Fam20A functions as an activator of Fam20C kinase activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing Fam20A enhances Fam20C activity without being catalytically active itself.

claim: Pre-incubation of Fam20A and Fam20C with ATP at 30°C did not increase subsequent ENAM phosphorylation when compared to conditions where pre-incubation was carried out on ice.
source: Pre-incubation of Fam20A and Fam20C with ATP at 30°C would allow Fam20C to phosphorylate Fam20A; however, this did not increase subsequent ENAM phosphorylation when compared to conditions where pre-incubation was carried out on ice (Figure 4E, group 2 and 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by pre-incubation experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: ENAM phosphorylation remained constant when Fam20A and Fam20C were pre-incubated with ATP or AMP-PCP.
source: Furthermore, ENAM phosphorylation remained constant when Fam20A and Fam20C were pre-incubated with ATP or AMP-PCP, a non-hydrolyzable ATP analogue (Figure 4E, group 3 and 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by pre-incubation experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The increase of substrate phosphorylation in the presence of Fam20A and Fam20C does not require Fam20C-dependent phosphorylation of Fam20A.
source: These findings suggest that the increase of substrate phosphorylation in the presence of Fam20A and Fam20C does not require Fam20C-dependent phosphorylation of Fam20A.
evidence: This is inferred from the pre-incubation experiments.

claim: Expression of Flag-tagged Fam20A D430A in Fam20A-KO ALCs increased Fam20C-dependent OPN phosphorylation similar to that of WT Fam20A.
source: Although mutation of the corresponding residue in Fam20C eliminated its kinase activity (Figure 1A), expression of Flag-tagged Fam20A D430A in Fam20A-KO ALCs increased Fam20C-dependent OPN phosphorylation similar to that of WT Fam20A (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rescue experiments shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Fam20A Q258E did not phosphorylate Fam20C.

claim: Fam20A Q258E was less potent than WT Fam20A to potentiate Fam20C-catalyzed ENAM phosphorylation.

claim: Fam20A increases the kinase activity of Fam20C in a catalytically independent manner.

claim: Fam20A and Fam20C co-eluted in nearly equal amounts in the higher molecular weight fractions during gel filtration.

claim: Fam20A and Fam20C form a complex of molar ratio of 1:1.

evidence: This is inferred from the gel filtration data showing equal amounts co-eluting.

claim: Fam20B and Fam20C did not co-elute during gel filtration.

claim: V5-tagged Fam20A could be co-immunoprecipitated with Flag-tagged Fam20C when stably co-expressed in U2OS cells.

claim: V5-tagged Fam20B could not be co-immunoprecipitated with Flag-tagged Fam20C when stably co-expressed in U2OS cells.

claim: Fam20A and Fam20C form a complex in vitro and in the secretory pathway of cells.

claim: Fam20C forms homodimers.

claim: Significant amounts of Fam20A protein were in fractions consistent with a dimer during gel filtration.

evidence: This is demonstrated by gel filtration analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Flag-tagged Fam20A co-immunoprecipitated with V5-tagged Fam20A when stably co-expressed in U2OS cells.

claim: Fam20A forms homodimers in cells.

claim: Analysis of the Fam20A/Fam20C complex by analytical ultracentrifugation revealed a molecular mass of 245 kDa.

claim: The Fam20A/Fam20C complex is a heterotetramer composed of two Fam20A and two Fam20C subunits.
source: Analysis of the Fam20A/Fam20C complex by analytical ultracentrifugation revealed a molecular mass of 245 kDa, which is consistent with a heterotetrameric complex composed of two Fam20A and two Fam20C subunits (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is inferred from the molecular mass determined by analytical ultracentrifugation.

claim: When Fam20A was added in excess to the in vitro kinase reaction, the kcat value of Fam20C for ENAM increased by 19-fold (from 0.04 s−1 to 0.76 s−1).
source: When Fam20A was added in excess to the in vitro kinase reaction to maximize complex formation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), the kcat value of Fam20C for ENAM increased by 19-fold (from 0.04 s−1 to 0.76 s−1), and the Km for ENAM decreased by ∼2.5-fold (from 14.6 μM to 5.6 μM) (Figure 5F).

claim: When Fam20A was added in excess to the in vitro kinase reaction, the Km of Fam20C for ENAM decreased by ∼2.5-fold (from 14.6 μM to 5.6 μM).
source: When Fam20A was added in excess to the in vitro kinase reaction to maximize complex formation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), the kcat value of Fam20C for ENAM increased by 19-fold (from 0.04 s−1 to 0.76 s−1), and the Km for ENAM decreased by ∼2.5-fold (from 14.6 μM to 5.6 μM) (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by kinetic analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The Fam20A/Fam20C complex catalyzed substrate phosphorylation much more efficiently than Fam20C alone.
source: This demonstrates that the Fam20A/Fam20C complex catalyzed substrate phosphorylation much more efficiently than Fam20C alone.

claim: Both Fam20A and Fam20C are localized in the Golgi and are secreted into the conditioned medium at comparable levels when expressed in mammalian cells.

claim: No redistribution of Flag-tagged Fam20C to the intracellular compartment was observed when co-expressed with V5-tagged Fam20A.

claim: Fam20A does not serve as a retention mechanism for the Fam20A/Fam20C complex.
source: These results suggest that Fam20A does not serve as a retention mechanism for the Fam20A/Fam20C complex.

claim: Fam20C is the bona fide kinase that phosphorylates casein.
source: Fam20C is the bona fide kinase that phosphorylates casein, one of the most abundant and highly phosphorylated proteins in milk (Tagliabracci et al., 2012).

claim: Casein is one of the most abundant and highly phosphorylated proteins in milk.
source: Fam20C is the bona fide kinase that phosphorylates casein, one of the most abundant and highly phosphorylated proteins in milk (Tagliabracci et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about milk composition.

claim: Fam20C and Fam20A mRNAs in the lactating mammary gland were dramatically elevated as compared to mammary gland from virgin animals.

claim: mRNA levels of Fam20B and other Fj family kinases remained relatively unaffected in lactating mammary gland compared to virgin animals.

claim: The relative increase in Fam20A and Fam20C mRNAs in lactating mammary gland were virtually identical.
source: Notably, the relative increase in Fam20A and Fam20C mRNAs in lactating mammary gland were virtually identical (Figure 6A).

claim: The expression patterns of Fam20A and Fam20C were largely consistent throughout the process of pregnancy and lactation.
source: In fact, the expression patterns of Fam20A and Fam20C were largely consistent throughout the process of pregnancy and lactation (Figure 6B).

claim: The mRNA levels of both Fam20A and Fam20C in the mammary gland gradually increased from 13 to 18 days of pregnancy and decreased during lactation and involution.
source: The mRNA levels of both Fam20A and Fam20C in the mammary gland gradually increased from 13 to 18 days of pregnancy and decreased during lactation and involution, with Fam20A peaking just before and Fam20C peaking just after the birth of the new litter (Figure 6B).

claim: Fam20A mRNA peaked just before the birth of the new litter.
source: The mRNA levels of both Fam20A and Fam20C in the mammary gland gradually increased from 13 to 18 days of pregnancy and decreased during lactation and involution, with Fam20A peaking just before and Fam20C peaking just after the birth of the new litter (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Fam20C mRNA peaked just after the birth of the new litter.
source: The mRNA levels of both Fam20A and Fam20C in the mammary gland gradually increased from 13 to 18 days of pregnancy and decreased during lactation and involution, with Fam20A peaking just before and Fam20C peaking just after the birth of the new litter (Figure 6B).

claim: Fam20A and Fam20C proteins could only be detected in the mammary glands of lactating, but not virgin mice.
source: Consistent with their mRNA levels, Fam20A and Fam20C proteins could only be detected in the mammary glands of lactating, but not virgin mice (Figure 6C).

claim: Coordinated expression of Fam20A and Fam20C is consistent with the idea that they function together in the mammary gland during pregnancy and lactation.
source: Coordinated expression of Fam20A and Fam20C is consistent with the idea that they function together in the mammary gland during pregnancy and lactation.

claim: Fam20A and Fam20C can form a functional complex in the mammary gland of pregnant/lactating animals.
source: These results demonstrate that Fam20A and Fam20C can form a functional complex in the mammary gland of pregnant/lactating animals.

claim: Expression of WT Fam20A, but not the AI mutants (L173R, G331D, D403N), markedly increased OPN phosphorylation in Fam20A-KO ALCs.

claim: Fam20A mutations L173R, G331D, and D403N likely interfere with the proper folding of Fam20A.

claim: Ectopic expression of Fam20A likely promoted not only Fam20C kinase activity, but also Fam20C stability.

claim: Fam20A could help stabilize Fam20C mutations.

source: In the Fam20A/Fam20C complex, Fam20C is catalytically active, whereas Fam20A functions as an allosteric activator to increase Fam20C kinase activity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by all the experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The formation of Fam20A/Fam20C complex may reflect an important mechanism to achieve high stoichiometry of secreted proteins phosphorylation.
source: Because the residual time of secreted proteins within the secretory pathway is limited, the formation of Fam20A/Fam20C complex, whose turnover number (kcat) is dramatically increased, may reflect an important mechanism to achieve high stoichiometry of secreted proteins phosphorylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetic data showing increased kcat of the complex.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in Fam20A result in inefficient phosphorylation of enamel matrix proteins by Fam20C.
source: Our model suggests that loss-of-function mutations in Fam20A result in inefficient phosphorylation of enamel matrix proteins by Fam20C, which prevents proper enamel formation and leads to AI.

claim: Inefficient phosphorylation of enamel matrix proteins by Fam20C prevents proper enamel formation and leads to AI.
source: Our model suggests that loss-of-function mutations in Fam20A result in inefficient phosphorylation of enamel matrix proteins by Fam20C, which prevents proper enamel formation and leads to AI.
evidence: This is the proposed model based on the experimental findings and clinical observations.

source: The degree of phosphorylation of enamel matrix proteins required for proper enamel formation is unknown.

source: However, patients with hypomorphic mutations in Fam20C, including T268M and P328S, survive infancy but developed dental defects (Fradin et al., 2011; Rafaelsen et al., 2013), indicating that optimal Fam20C activity is critical for enamel formation.

claim: Optimal Fam20C activity is critical for enamel formation.

claim: Discovery of the Fam20A-Fam20C pair extends the concept that the activity of a kinase can be allosterically regulated by dimerization with an inactive paralog.
source: Discovery of the Fam20A-Fam20C pair extends the concept that the activity of a kinase can be allosterically regulated by dimerization with an inactive paralog, which further expands the pseudokinase-kinase mode of regulation to protein phosphorylation within the secretory pathway.
evidence: This is the conceptual contribution of the work.

claim: The pseudokinase-kinase mode of regulation is expanded to protein phosphorylation within the secretory pathway by the discovery of the Fam20A-Fam20C pair.
